prompt:
You are a blind code reader in an empirical software-engineering study. Work only from the files in the current directory.

1. Read protocol.md first.
2. Read batch.md. It names 20 Java files by id, their path in their repository, and their local copy under files/.
3. For every file: read the whole file (use Read with offset and limit for files over 2000 lines, do not skip the tail). Identify the method with the highest cognitive complexity (the one with the most and deepest nested branches, loops and boolean chains) and name it. Then answer Q1, Q2, Q3 and Q4 from the protocol as true or false, each with one sentence of evidence from the file, and write a one-line note of the form "methodName: what it does". Do NOT derive or state the category; the mapping is applied later.
4. Blindness: do not try to read anything outside the current directory and do not try to find out anything about these classes beyond the file itself.
5. Answer with one entry per id of the batch, all 20 of them, in the required JSON form.

readings.note: read(byte[],int,int): fills the caller's array from the internal buffer and the source stream, bypassing the buffer when unmarked and the request is large

evidence.q1: lookupNamespaceURI walks from the namespacing element up through containing elements, checking each node's own prefix/namespace and its xmlns/xmlns:prefix attributes with nested for/if/for/if and ternaries, and returns the resolved URI.
evidence.q2: All methods implement the W3C Node contract for a DOM node (children stubs, names, base URI, namespace lookup, equality, user data).
evidence.q3: It traverses the DOM tree of Node objects it is itself part of (ancestors, attributes), a tree structure akin to a syntax tree, so the lookups are its own namespace-resolution behaviour rather than borrowed foreign data.
evidence.q4: Several methods (setNodeValue, getBaseURI, setTextContent, getNamespacingElement) switch over getNodeType(), but the top method lookupNamespaceURI is a nested traversal loop, not a case table.

readings.note: lookupNamespaceURI: resolves a namespace prefix (or default namespace) by walking ancestor elements and their xmlns attributes

evidence.q1: startRequest derives the Cronet request from the connection's own state (doOutput, method, mOutputStream, mRequestHeaders, useCaches, traffic tag/uid), adding default Content-Length/Content-Type headers and setting method, mRequest and connected, i.e. the connection's own protocol step.
evidence.q2: All methods serve one concept: implementing HttpURLConnection semantics on top of a Cronet UrlRequest (request headers, output streams, response blocking, header maps, callback).
evidence.q3: It works almost entirely on its own fields (mRequestHeaders, mResponseInfo, mOutputStream, connected); the only depth-2 chain is mOutputStream.getUploadDataProvider().getLength().
evidence.q4: startRequest is a sequence of separate if guards (doOutput, GET→POST, output stream present, Content-Length, Content-Type, caches, traffic stats) plus a header loop, not a case chain over one value.

readings.note: startRequest: builds and starts the Cronet UrlRequest from the connection's method, headers, upload stream and traffic-stats settings

evidence.q1: generateThumbnailFunction's switchOnFirst lambda parses the thumb spec into either width_height integers or a percentage scale, validates them (parts.length == 2, 0 < scale < 1) and returns the corresponding thumbnail flux or an error.
evidence.q2: Every method (generateThumbnailFunction, two generateThumbnail overloads, generateThumbnailInternal, initPipedOutputStream, closeStream) serves one concept: producing thumbnail image streams.
evidence.q3: It works on its own thumb string and DataBuffer streams and uses Thumbnails as a library; no getter chains or copying between other objects.
evidence.q4: The complexity is nested if guards on signal value, thumb format and scale range, not a case chain over kinds.

readings.note: generateThumbnailFunction: returns a function that, on first signal, parses the thumb spec (W_H or percent) and scales the image flux accordingly

evidence.q1: parse takes the site frame and populates the parser's own collections (stopPlaces, multiModalStopPlaces, quays, tariffZones, parkings, ...) through its own parseX methods, guarded by null checks and feature flags, then warns on unmapped sections.
evidence.q2: All methods serve one concept: extracting site entities from a NeTEx Site frame into the parser's collections and handing them to the entity index.
evidence.q3: The chains frame.getStopPlaces().getStopPlace_() etc. are on generated JAXB model objects (data holders), so by the convention they are not foreign data.
evidence.q4: parse's complexity is separate if conditions guarding calls (five guards with && on feature flags), explicitly not a dispatch table; parseStopPlaces has one if/else.

readings.note: parse: collects stop places, groups, flexible stops, tariff zones, quays and parkings from a NeTEx Site frame into the parser's collections

evidence.q1: determineCompleteType loops down nested parameter_id contexts until the one holding the name, wrapping the accumulated type string in parentheses with pointer and suffix tokens, and returns the complete C type string.
evidence.q2: createNew, addParameter and determineCompleteType all serve one concept: building a ParameterList AST node from the parser's parameter declarations.
evidence.q3: It reads ANTLR parse-tree contexts (parameter_id.ptrs(), type_suffix(), parameter_name()), which are syntax-tree data holders, to compute its own string.
evidence.q4: The complexity is a while loop with two ifs inside and two ifs after, not a switch over kinds.

readings.note: determineCompleteType: reconstructs a parameter's complete C type string from nested parameter_id parse-tree contexts (pointers, suffixes)

evidence.q1: unzipXWalkZip iterates the zip entries, finds XWalkRuntimeLib.apk, deletes stale temp/final files, copies the entry bytes in a read/write loop to a temp file, renames it, and deletes the archive, i.e. an extraction procedure over its own inputs.
evidence.q2: All methods (downUrl, saveZipFile, xWalkLibExist, tryUseXWalk, checkEmbedded, unzipXWalkZip, getRuntimeAbi, extractXWalkLib, path helpers) serve one concept: provisioning and initialising the Crosswalk (XWalk) runtime.
evidence.q3: It works on files, zip entries and reflection results it obtains itself; there are no getter chains or copying between other behaviour-bearing objects.
evidence.q4: unzipXWalkZip is while/if-else/if/if/if/while nesting over zip entries; the small switch on ABI strings in getRuntimeAbi is not the top method.

readings.note: unzipXWalkZip: extracts XWalkRuntimeLib.apk from the downloaded Crosswalk zip into the app cache and deletes the zip

evidence.q1: checkAllNodesHealth (inside the heartbeat Task in startHeartbeat) queries running nodes, drops non-ZStack UUIDs, compares each heartbeat against the DB clock and the computed delta to fill its own suspects list, detects time regression, and reconciles the hash ring, i.e. the liveness-detection procedure.
evidence.q2: The class bootstraps the node via a flow chain (start), handles bus messages (handleMessage), runs DB heartbeat and peer failure detection (startHeartbeat), propagates node join/left events, installs shutdown hooks and debug-signal dumps, and orchestrates stop: several distinct concerns.
evidence.q3: It decides on ManagementNodeVO rows (data holders) and its own node/suspects state; the only depth-2 chain is destinationMaker.getNodeInfo(nodeUuid).getNodeIP().
evidence.q4: The complexity is a for loop over nodes with several if/continue guards and two forEach lambdas, with no switch over kinds; message dispatch in handleLocalMessage is tiny.

readings.note: checkAllNodesHealth (heartbeat task in startHeartbeat): scans ManagementNodeVO heartbeats, marks stale peers as suspects, fires time-regression events and reconciles the hash ring

evidence.q1: service(url) only matches the url against about fifteen path patterns, extracts ids with StringUtils.subString, and returns the result of the matching getXxx helper; it computes nothing itself.
evidence.q2: The Javadoc and methods describe one concept: aggregating Druid monitoring data (datasource, SQL, wall, web URI, session, spring stats) across service instances discovered from the registry.
evidence.q3: It copies ServiceInstance host/port/serviceId into ServiceNode and node name/address into ContentBean, but these are DTOs/data holders, and the aggregation logic is this service's own.
evidence.q4: service is one long if chain over url prefixes/suffixes (serviceList.json, /datasource.json, /datasource-, /connectionInfo-, /sql.json, /wall.json, /serviceId, /weburi.json, /weburi-, /webapp.json, /websession.json, /websession-, /spring.json, /spring-detail.json), each branch one to four lines.

readings.note: service: routes a Druid console URL to the matching stat-aggregation helper by prefix/suffix matching and returns its JSON

evidence.q1: parseResponse decodes the Clarity JSON array into a SysClarityData entity, reading metricName and the first information object and converting counts and rankings into entity fields.
evidence.q2: fetchAndSave, updateStatus, parseResponse and toJsonRanking all serve one concept: fetching Clarity insights and persisting them as a SysClarityData row.
evidence.q3: It reads JSONObject values and sets fields on a SysClarityData entity, both plain data holders, and the two mappers are used as repositories.
evidence.q4: parseResponse's complexity is mainly the switch on metricName with nine cases (Traffic, ScrollDepth, DeadClickCount, RageClickCount, Device, PopularPages, ReferrerUrl, PageTitle, Browser), each one to three lines, inside a loop with two null guards.

readings.note: parseResponse: maps the Clarity API metrics array into SysClarityData fields via a switch on metricName

evidence.q1: Type.getDescriptor(StringBuilder, Class) encodes a Class into its JVM descriptor: loops peeling array dimensions, maps primitives to their letter, and writes L<internal name>; for objects, replacing dots with slashes.
evidence.q2: The class (with its embedded ASM Type copy) does one thing: compute the JVM descriptor string of a Constructor or Method.
evidence.q3: It works on java.lang.Class and reflection metadata (data) to build its own StringBuilder; no getter chains on behaviour-bearing objects.
evidence.q4: Over half of the method's complexity is the nine-way if/else-if chain over d == Integer.TYPE, Void.TYPE, Boolean.TYPE, ... each case a single char assignment, wrapped in a while/if/else-if/else for arrays and objects.

readings.note: Type.getDescriptor(StringBuilder, Class): appends the JVM type descriptor of a class (primitive letter, [ for arrays, L...; for objects)

evidence.q1: onTouch handles the touch protocol over the attacher's own zoom state: on ACTION_DOWN it disallows parent intercept and cancels the fling, on UP/CANCEL it snaps back when getScale() < mMinScale by posting an AnimatedZoomRunnable, then feeds the detectors and computes the returned handled flag.
evidence.q2: All methods (scale bounds, matrix bookkeeping, checkMatrixBounds, updateBaseMatrix, gesture callbacks, fling and zoom runnables) serve one concept: zoom/pan gesture control of an ImageView's display matrix.
evidence.q3: It reads the ImageView's drawable, bounds, padding and parent, but the complexity lives in its own matrices (mBaseMatrix, mSuppMatrix), scale limits and edge state; the one depth-2 chain is imageView.getDrawable().getIntrinsicWidth().
evidence.q4: onTouch's switch on ev.getAction() has only two cases, and the rest of its complexity is separate && guards around detector calls; checkMatrixBounds' switches on mScaleType are small.

readings.note: onTouch: handles touch events for the zoomable ImageView (parent intercept, fling cancel, snap-back below min scale, delegate to tap and scale/drag detectors)

evidence.q1: map iterates the flexible stop place's areas, skips unsupported or invalid geometries with issues, chooses per area between finding regular stops inside the geometry and creating an AreaStop, and returns a built GroupStop (or null).
evidence.q2: map, mapFlexArea, findStopsInFlexArea, mapGeometry, mapTransitMode and the key-list helpers all serve one concept: mapping NeTEx FlexibleStopPlace into OTP stop locations.
evidence.q3: The chains flexibleStopPlace.getAreas().getFlexibleAreaOrFlexibleAreaRefOrHailAndRideArea() and getName().getValue() are on generated JAXB model objects (data holders), and the output is built via the site repository builder.
evidence.q4: map's complexity is a for loop with instanceof/continue, null/continue and an if/else on shouldAddStopsFromArea, not a case chain over kinds.

readings.note: map: converts a NeTEx FlexibleStopPlace's areas into regular stops or AreaStops and groups them into a GroupStop
